description: Hericium erinaceus is a toothed fungus that forms a single rounded, unbranched white cushion bearing long, cascading, icicle-like spines. It is prized as a choice edible with a seafood-like (crab or lobster) flavor and texture, and is studied for compounds (hericenones and erinacines) reported to stimulate nerve growth factor (NGF) synthesis in laboratory settings.
edibilityNotes: Choice edible, best cooked; flesh is sliced and sauteed, developing a seafood-like flavor. Cook thoroughly before eating. Harvest while white and firm; older yellowing or browning specimens turn sour and unpleasant. As with all wild fungi, confirm identity before consuming.
habitat: wounds and scars on living hardwoods
distribution: Widespread across temperate forests of the Northern Hemisphere, including North America, Europe, and East Asia.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Hericium coralloides
dangerousLookalikes.note: Coral tooth fungus: much-branched with spines clustered along the branches, rather than a single unbranched cushion of long hanging spines. Also edible, so not a safety hazard.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Hericium americanum
dangerousLookalikes.note: Bear's head tooth: branched with longer spines than H. coralloides. Also edible; distinguished by its branching habit versus the single unbranched mass of H. erinaceus.
